evidence.quote: There was a short-term rehab bed available, but it needed one more day for insurance pre-authorization. The alternative was finalizing home discharge that same day... So finishing the extra checks felt like it would cost more than it was worth if it meant putting him through that.

evidence.quote: My job was to figure out, does he go home with some outpatient support, or does he need a short-term rehab stay first.

ambiguities: A3.1 (serving/attending) versus A3.5 (caring): the bedside conversation and daughter calls could be classified as either responsive service or welfare-oriented caring; both are present but caring is more textually supported at the decision point involving patient distress.

A3.3 (selling/influencing) is plausible when discussing the patient's reaction to the delay ('I mentioned it might just be the one night... he actually said he supposed he could manage'), but the text shows persuasion attempt rather than a completed negotiation, so it was not elevated to secondary.
